herdr plugin action invoke example.layout.apply
herdr plugin pane open --plugin example.layout --entrypoint board
herdr plugin log list --plugin example.layout
```

`plugin install` accepts GitHub shorthand only, such as
`owner/repo/subdir`. It clones with `git`, shows a preview in interactive
terminals, runs supported build commands, then stores the checkout under
Herdr-managed plugin data and registers it. Use `--yes` for noninteractive
installs. Reinstalling a GitHub-managed plugin replaces that managed checkout.
Installed and linked plugins, including their enabled state, are global to the
current user and available in every Herdr session. Both `plugin install` and
`plugin link` can register plugins while no Herdr server is running. Plugins
installed only in a named session on Herdr 0.7.3 must be installed or linked
again. Existing plugin config and state remain in place.
Installing over a locally linked plugin is refused; unlink or uninstall the
local plugin first. `plugin install` and `plugin link` create the plugin's
config and state directories, and `plugin config-dir <id>` prints the config
directory for setup docs and shell scripts.

`plugin uninstall <id-or-source>` unregisters the plugin. For GitHub-managed
installs it also removes the managed checkout, and it accepts either the plugin
id or the same `owner/repo[/subdir...]` shorthand used by install.
`plugin unlink <id>` only unregisters a plugin and leaves files alone, which is
useful for local development. There is no separate `plugin update` in v1;
reinstall from GitHub to refresh a managed plugin.

The example cookbook repo is `ogulcancelik/herdr-plugin-examples`. It contains
separate example plugins in subdirectories, including `agent-telegram-notify`,
`github-link-preview`, and `dev-layout-bootstrap`. Use them as examples to copy;
Herdr does not maintain them as official plugins.

## Build commands

Build commands run during GitHub `plugin install` after confirmation and before
Herdr registers the plugin. If a build command fails, install aborts and the
plugin is not registered. `plugin link` does not run build commands; local
authors build their working tree themselves. Build commands may generate files,
but changing `herdr-plugin.toml` after the install preview aborts install. Build
failures show the plugin id, build index, working directory, command, exit
status or spawn error, and capped stdout/stderr without interpreting tool output.

Build commands are plain argv commands too, but they do not receive runtime
plugin context or Herdr socket env. Plugin authors should document required
system tools such as `cargo`, `npm`, `bun`, or `lua`; Herdr reports build
failures but does not install missing toolchains.

The marketplace helps you discover plugins. Install any plugin straight from

content.text:
I haven't changed anything yet. Below is the plan, built from the code and from probing your live herdr 0.9.0 socket. (The `coder_report_task` tool your CLAUDE.md mentions isn't available in this session, so I couldn't send status updates through it.)

## What herdr gives us

- **No built-in form or picker.** The only "herdr modal" is a plugin pane opened as a popup (`placement = "popup"`). It's the same mechanism `show` already uses. So the configure modal will be our own small TUI running in a herdr popup.
- **It already knows which harnesses are installed.** `integration.list` returns each one with `available: true|false` (whether its command is on PATH). On this box that's claude, codex, opencode and hermes. That works on anyone's machine, so it's our discovery source, with a PATH scan if the call fails.
- **The pane snapshot already covers most of what the bridge adds.** It has `agent`, `agent_status`, `agent_session`, `cwd` and the terminal title per pane. The Claude transcript reader already finds its file through herdr's `agent_session`.

## Part 1: use any available harness for the recap

Today `claude` and `codex` are hard-coded in five places: the `Backend` type, `summarizerOf`, the `summarizerFor` switch, the `backend` command in `bin/`, and two manifest actions.

1. **One table of harness profiles** (`src/adapters/harnesses.ts`). Each entry holds the harness id, its command, how to build the arguments, how the instructions go in (a system-prompt flag or prepended to stdin), how the answer comes out (a JSON field, an `-o` file, or plain stdout), and its default model. A single `CliSummarizer` runs any profile. The existing `ClaudeSummarizer` and `CodexSummarizer` become two entries, keeping their behaviour exactly.
2. **Profiles to ship:** claude and codex (proven today), plus opencode and hermes (installed here; I'll check their headless flags before adding them). There's also a **custom** profile: `TAB_RECAP_CUSTOM_CMD`, any command that reads the prompt on stdin and prints Markdown. That makes "any agent" true without guessing every CLI's flags.
3. **Config:** `TAB_RECAP_BACKEND=auto|<id>`. `auto` picks the first available harness in a preference order. Models are stored per harness as `TAB_RECAP_MODEL_<ID>`; the old `CLAUDE_MODEL` and `CODEX_MODEL` keys keep working. `Backend` changes from a two-value union to a branded id, checked against the profile table.
4. **Discovery port:** `Harnesses.available(): Available | Unknown`, backed by `integration.list` through `herdr-fleet.ts` (the only file allowed to talk to the herdr socket), falling back to PATH.

## Part 2: the configure modal

A new manifest pane `setup` opens as a popup, through a new action `tab-recap.configure`. It replaces the separate `backend-claude` and `backend-codex` actions; the `backend <id> [model]` command stays for scripts.

```text
┌ Tab Recap · who writes the recap ───────────┐
│ ▸ ● claude    haiku           ✓ current     │
│   ● codex     gpt-6-luna                    │
│   ● opencode  (default)                     │
│   ● hermes    (default)                     │
│   ○ gemini    not on PATH                   │
│   ◇ custom    TAB_RECAP_CUSTOM_CMD          │
│ model: haiku_          words: 450           │
│ ↑↓ pick · ⏎ save · t test · m model · q     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- `t` runs a tiny test recap and shows how long it took and what it cost, or the error. You find out a harness is broken here, not in the column.
- Saving writes through the existing `setValues` (so comments in `config.env` survive) and applies from the next recap.
- The key handling is a pure function, tested like the fold. The popup process is its own composition root under `src/setup/`. If herdr says `ui_busy`, the command falls back to printing what to run.
- **First run:** if `auto` finds no harness, the daemon shows one toast (`notification.show`) telling you to run *Tab Recap: configure*, instead of failing silently on every turn.

## Part 3: does it work without the bridge? (your GitHub question)

**It already degrades without crashing.** I traced it:
- The column's bridge read fails, the alert is treated as absent, and no alert header is drawn.
- `heal()` does nothing while there's no heartbeat file, so `systemctl` is never called.

**But the coupling is real and would confuse a GitHub user:**

| # | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The default bridge dir is set to `~/.local/state/atalaya-bridge` and healing defaults to `1`, so the bridge is opt-out. | Make it opt-in: empty by default. Heal only when explicitly turned on. |
| 2 | `column/main.ts`, `daemon/main.ts` and `bin` create `AtalayaBridge` directly, and the render code imports the bridge's `Alert` type. | Add an optional enrichment port that returns a per-lane "work line". The default comes from herdr: `agent_status` plus how long it's been in that state (the board already tracks that), and branch/dirty from `git -C <pane cwd>`. The bridge becomes one optional adapter for it. |
| 3 | Healing uses `systemctl --user`, which is Linux-only, but the manifest lists `macos`. | Only possible with the bridge adapter on; document it as Linux-only. |
| 4 | Only claude and codex panes get a column. `policy.kinds` defaults to `claude,codex` and only those two have transcript readers. An opencode, gemini or cursor pane gets nothing. | Optional: a fallback reader that uses herdr's `pane.read` (`recent_unwrapped`) for any agent herdr detects. It's still read-only, but its cursor would be a hash of the last line instead of a byte position, so recaps are noisier. |
| 5 | The repo README "House rules", CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, the manifest description and two lint rules mention atalaya-bridge and delivery-handbook, which outsiders can't see. | Reword for the public. Keep the bridge as an "optional integration" section. |

**Publishing:** set up a GitLab push mirror (Settings → Repository → Mirroring, GitHub fine-grained token, protected branches only, so just `main`). Then add the GitHub topic `herdr-plugin`; the marketplace picks up manifests in subfolders. People install with `herdr plugin install <owner>/herdr-plugins/tab-recap`. We have no build step and no runtime dependencies, so a GitHub install works as-is. Run one secret/path scan before the first push, because the history becomes public.

## Order of work

1. Harness table, `CliSummarizer` and the discovery port, with tests. The current claude/codex behaviour must stay identical.
2. Setup popup, the configure action and the first-run toast.
3. Bridge becomes opt-in, herdr-native work line, docs and lint rules cleaned up.
4. *(If you want it)* fallback reader for any agent.
5. Secret scan, push mirror, GitHub topic, install test from GitHub on a clean machine.

## Decisions I need from you

1. **Scope of "any harness":** only the recap writer (parts 1–2), or also give a column to panes running opencode, gemini, etc. (item 4)? I recommend the writer now and item 4 as a later step.
2. **Profiles:** claude, codex, opencode, hermes plus custom, or should I also research gemini, cursor-agent, qwen and copilot headless flags now?
3. **Default backend:** `auto` (first available, in the order claude → codex → opencode → hermes), or keep `claude` fixed?
4. **Bridge on the public mirror:** keep it as an opt-in adapter in the public code, or strip it there and keep it only on GitLab? I recommend keeping it opt-in, since one codebase is simpler.
5. **GitHub repo:** which owner/name, and should I set up the mirror, or will you?

I can also put this on a one-screen page with a diagram if that's easier to review.

content.text:
You can have the two branches, the Spanish/English UI and a recap-language setting. The branch setup needs one rule to stay manageable, explained below. Still a plan; I haven't changed any code.

## Two branches

```text
main ──●──●──●──●──────●──→  push-mirrored to GitHub (public)
        \     \         \
atalaya  ●─────●─────────●─→  stays on GitLab
          (main + bridge adapter + homelab defaults)
```

- **`main` is the GitHub branch.** It's the plain-herdr plugin, with no bridge, systemd or homelab paths. A GitLab push mirror set to protected branches only copies just this branch.
- **`atalaya` = `main` plus a small fixed set of extra files.** Changes only flow from `main` into `atalaya`, never the other way. Every fix lands on `main` first, then `atalaya` merges it.
- **The rule that keeps this cheap: `atalaya` only adds files and never edits shared ones.** I'll build one extension point on `main`, `src/extensions/index.ts`, which exports an empty list. On `atalaya` that one file lists the bridge adapter, and the branch adds:
  - `src/adapters/atalaya-bridge.ts`
  - the bridge port
  - `config.atalaya.env` with your current defaults (bridge dir, healing on)
  - a docs page

  Merging `main` into `atalaya` then conflicts in at most one file.
- **A CI job on `atalaya`** checks that the branch is never behind `main` and that its diff from `main` touches only those files. Without that check, the two branches drift apart within a few weeks.

## Spanish/English UI

- **String tables with no dependencies:** `src/i18n/en.ts` holds every visible string, and `es.ts` has to be typed the same way. A missing Spanish string then stops the type check, the same way a missing intent does now.
- **What gets translated:** column headings, the bar, status labels, "no recap yet…", the configure modal, and the `bin` messages.
- **Time:** "2m ago" vs "hace 2 min" uses Node's built-in `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, so still no runtime dependencies.
- **Setting:** `TAB_RECAP_LOCALE=auto|en|es`. `auto` reads `LC_ALL`/`LANG`. You can change it in the modal.
- **Limit:** herdr's manifest action titles are fixed text and can't be translated at runtime. I'll keep them in English (or write them in both languages, e.g. `Tab Recap: configure · configurar`).

## Recap language

- **Setting:** `TAB_RECAP_RECAP_LANG=ui|en|es`. `ui` means "same as the UI". The modal gets a second row to pick it.
- **There's a catch, found in the code:** the phone bar finds its headline by looking for the `## Waiting on you` and `## Now` headings (`present.ts:153`). A Spanish recap would have `## Esperando tu respuesta` instead, and the bar would go blank.
  - **Fix:** one table of sections with a stable id and both labels (`waiting` → *Waiting on you* / *Esperando tu respuesta*). The prompt is generated from that table, and the bar matches the heading in either language.
- **Switching mid-session:** recaps build on the previous one, so the prompt will say "rewrite the whole recap in Spanish". The first recap after a switch is fully in the new language, not mixed.
- **Your current agents' text stays as it is.** Only the recap is translated.

## New words for CONTEXT.md

- **Locale:** the UI language.
- **Recap language:** what the recap is written in.
- **Extension:** an optional adapter that a branch adds to the extension list.

The vocabulary lint rule needs these added before the code uses them.

## Revised order of work

1. **Extension point plus moving the bridge out.** `main` becomes bridge-free, the `atalaya` branch is created, and the CI check is added.
2. **Harness table and discovery** (unchanged from the last plan).
3. **i18n:** string tables, locale setting, both-language section table, Spanish prompt.
4. **Configure modal:** pick harness, UI language and recap language, plus the test-recap key.
5. **Docs** in both languages, then the GitHub mirror and a clean install test from GitHub.

## Decisions I need from you

1. **Branch names:** `main` (public/GitHub) and `atalaya`, with changes only flowing from `main` into `atalaya`? Or do you literally want a branch called `github`?
2. **Recap language:** only English/Spanish, or also a free-text choice (e.g. "Portuguese") passed straight to the model? The headings would stay English or Spanish.
3. **README:** two files (`README.md` and `README.es.md`), or English only on GitHub?
4. **The earlier five questions are still open,** especially scope (the recap writer only, or also columns for other agents) and the default harness (`auto` or fixed `claude`).

Once you answer, I'll start with step 1, since everything else is built on top of the branch split.

entries.name: EnterPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

1. Focus on understanding the user's request and the code associated with their request. Actively search for existing functions, utilities, and patterns that can be reused — avoid proposing new code when suitable implementations already exist.

2. **Launch up to 3 Explore agents IN PARALLEL** (single message, multiple tool calls) to efficiently explore the codebase.

   - Use multiple agents when: the scope is uncertain, multiple areas of the codebase are involved, or you need to understand existing patterns before planning.
   - Quality over quantity - 3 agents maximum, but you should try to use the minimum number of agents necessary (usually just 1)
   - If using multiple agents: Provide each agent with a specific search focus or area to explore. Example: One agent searches for existing implementations, another explores related components, a third investigating testing patterns

### Phase 2: Design
Goal: Design an implementation approach.

Launch Plan agent(s) to design the implementation based on the user's intent and your exploration results from Phase 1.

You can launch up to 1 agent(s) in parallel.

- Name the critical files to be modified. For changes that repeat a pattern across many files, describe the pattern once and list a few representative paths — do not enumerate every file or line number
- Reference existing functions and utilities you found that should be reused, with their file paths
- Include a verification section describing how to test the changes end-to-end (run the code, use MCP tools, run tests)

### Phase 5: Call ExitPlanMode
At the very end of your turn, once you have asked the user questions and are happy with your final plan file - you should always call ExitPlanMode to indicate to the user that you are done planning.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tab-recap's lint gate. Exit: 0 clean · 1 a finding · 3 could not look (a tool is missing).
set -uo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$HERE"

command -v ast-grep >/dev/null || { echo "lint: 3 — NOT COVERED: ast-grep is not on PATH" >&2; exit 3; }
[ -x node_modules/.bin/tsgo ] && [ -x node_modules/.bin/oxlint ] \
    || { echo "lint: 3 — NOT COVERED: run 'npm install' (tsgo, oxlint)" >&2; exit 3; }

failures=0
fail() { echo "  FAIL  $*"; failures=$((failures + 1)); }

echo "rules (ast-grep) — each must pass on the tree AND bite its bad probe:"
mapfile -t RULES < <(find rules -maxdepth 1 -name '*.yml' | sort)
[ "${#RULES[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "lint: 3 — NOT COVERED: zero rules" >&2; exit 3; }
for rule in "${RULES[@]}"; do
    id="$(basename "$rule" .yml)"
    probes="rules/probes/$id"
    [ -f "$probes/bad.ts" ] && [ -f "$probes/good.ts" ] || { fail "$id — no bad/good probe"; continue; }
    ast-grep scan --rule "$rule" src bin test >/dev/null 2>&1 || { ast-grep scan --rule "$rule" src bin test; fail "$id — the tree breaks it"; continue; }
    ast-grep scan --rule "$rule" "$probes/bad.ts" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { fail "$id — its bad probe does not trigger it: the rule does not bite"; continue; }
    ast-grep scan --rule "$rule" "$probes/good.ts" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { fail "$id — its good probe triggers it: the rule over-reaches"; continue; }
    echo "  ok    $id"
done

echo "vocabulary — every banned word in the rule is documented in CONTEXT.md:"
banned="$(grep -oE '\(\?i\)\([a-z|]+\)' rules/recap-vocabulary.yml | sed -E 's/^\(\?i\)\(|\)$//g' | tr '|' ' ')"
for word in $banned; do
    grep -q "\`$word\`" CONTEXT.md && echo "  ok    $word" || fail "'$word' is banned but CONTEXT.md does not say what replaces it"
done

echo "typecheck (tsgo, strict + exactOptionalPropertyTypes + erasableSyntaxOnly):"
node_modules/.bin/tsgo --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && echo "  ok    tsgo" || fail "tsgo"

echo "oxlint (type-aware, the atalaya-bridge configuration):"
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --type-aware . && echo "  ok    oxlint" || fail "oxlint"

echo "the linters bite (a seeded violation must fail them):"
bash ci/verify-bite.sh && echo "  ok    tsgo and oxlint both reject the seed" || fail "a linter accepted the seeded violation"

[ "$failures" -eq 0 ] && { echo "lint: clean"; exit 0; }
echo "lint: $failures finding(s)"; exit 1

id: recap-no-foreign-write
language: typescript
severity: error
message: >-
  Only adapters write files, and only under the plugin's own state dir. The domain,
  the application, the render layer, the ports, the transport and the column
  never call a filesystem write.
note: >-
  Transcripts and atalaya-bridge's outbox are READ-ONLY to this plugin. Every write
  goes through the RecapStore port (fs-recap-store.ts) or the Pidfile adapter.
files:
  - "**/src/recap/**"
  - "**/src/ports/**"
  - "**/src/transport/**"
  - "**/src/column/**"
  - "**/probes/recap-no-foreign-write/**"
rule:
  any:
    - pattern: writeFileSync($$$)
    - pattern: appendFileSync($$$)
    - pattern: rmSync($$$)
    - pattern: mkdirSync($$$)
    - pattern: renameSync($$$)
    - pattern: writeFile($$$)
    - pattern: appendFile($$$)
id: recap-vocabulary
language: typescript
severity: error
message: >-
  Banned synonym in an identifier. CONTEXT.md is the vocabulary: summary -> recap,
  sidebar/panel -> column, offset -> cursor, worker -> daemon.
note: >-
  Words from the outside world (Claude's `away_summary`, a herdr field) may appear
  as STRING LITERALS at an adapter's edge — never as our own names.
files:
  - "**/src/**"
  - "**/bin/**"
  - "**/test/**"
  - "**/probes/recap-vocabulary/**"
rule:
  any:
    - kind: identifier
    - kind: property_identifier
    - kind: type_identifier
    - kind: shorthand_property_identifier
    - kind: shorthand_property_identifier_pattern
  regex: "(?i)(summary|sidebar|panel|offset|worker)"

Pure key-reducer tested. First-run toast via notification.show when auto finds no harness.
D) i18n en/es: typed catalogs src/i18n/en.ts + es.ts (`es: Messages`), TAB_RECAP_LOCALE=auto|en|es (auto from LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES/LANG). Render (src/recap/render/present.ts) takes Messages. Extensions read their own config keys via a get(key) passed in. Column (src/column/main.ts) and daemon iterate extensions. Lint rules/docs mentioning the bridge become generic. A CI guard on atalaya checks main is an ancestor and the diff stays within an allowlist (ci/atalaya-files.txt). Root .gitlab-ci.yml runs lint+test.

Specifically check: does putting the extension registry under src/extensions/ conflict with existing rules (recap-layers-no-io, recap-transport-boundary, recap-no-foreign-write file globs)? Does `test/present.test.ts` / other tests need updates? Any issue with the 128KiB argv limit (MAX_ARG_STRLEN) for argv-based harnesses given EXCERPT_BUDGET=60_000 chars in src/recap/application/recap-job.ts? Anything in bin/tab-recap.ts, herdr-plugin.toml, README.md, config.example.env that I must change?

# tab-recap: any harness, configure modal, en/es, and a public `main` without the bridge

## Context

`tab-recap` (herdr plugin, `/home/coder/homelab/herdr-plugins/tab-recap`) writes a rolling recap per
tab, but the summarizer is hard-wired to `claude`/`codex`, configuration is two fixed actions, every
string is English, and the code is coupled to the homelab-only atalaya-bridge (defaults pointing at
`~/.local/state/atalaya-bridge`, heal on via `systemctl --user`). The operator wants to publish the
plugin on GitHub (herdr marketplace) as a mirror of GitLab `main`, keep an `atalaya` flavour for the
homelab, pick the harness from a herdr modal, and have a Spanish/English UI plus a selectable recap
language.

Decisions taken (operator, 2026-10-04): branches **`main` (public) + `atalaya`**, flow main → atalaya
only · harnesses **claude, codex, opencode, hermes + custom** · recap language **en / es / free text**
· scope **recap writer only** (columns stay for claude/codex lanes) · default backend **`auto`** ·
docs **English only** · GitLab/GitHub paths **given later** (mirror is the last step).

Facts measured on herdr 0.9.0 that shape the design:
- herdr has no native form/select UI; a "modal" is a plugin pane with `placement = "popup"` (what
  `HerdrFleet.show` already does). Popup returns `ui_busy` while another herdr modal is open.
- `integration.list` RPC returns `{target, label, command, available, state}` per agent —
  `available` = command on PATH. Here: claude, codex, opencode, hermes. This is discovery.
- `notification.show {title, body}` exists for a first-run toast.
- opencode: `opencode run [message..] --pure -m provider/model --format json`; hermes:
  `hermes -z PROMPT --ignore-rules --ignore-user-config -m MODEL --usage-file PATH` (prints only the
  final text). Both take the prompt as argv → input mode `argv` with a byte cap (MAX_ARG_STRLEN 128 KiB).
- Without the bridge the plugin already degrades (read → `absent`, heal no-ops without a heartbeat);
  the work is removing the coupling, not fixing a crash.
- Repo has **no commits yet** → the first commit on `main` can already be the public tree, so the
  public history never contains the bridge.

## Step 0 — Branch model (built into the code, not just git)

- New generic **Extension** port `src/ports/extension.ts`:
  `{ id; notes?(): NotesResult /* Map<pane, Note{label, at, details[]}> | Unknown */; warning?(m: Messages): string | null; upkeep?(): Promise<UpkeepResult> }`.
  Extensions read their own keys through a `get(key)` handed in (config.ts never learns their keys).
- Registry `src/extensions/index.ts` exports `extensions(get) => []` on `main`. **This is the only
  shared file `atalaya` edits.**
- `atalaya` adds: `src/extensions/atalaya-bridge.ts` (today's `adapters/atalaya-bridge.ts` + the
  `Alert` type from `ports/bridge.ts`, mapped to `Note`), `test/atalaya-bridge.test.ts`,
  `ATALAYA.md`, `config.atalaya.example.env` (bridge dir, heal=1).
- `ci/branch-guard.sh` (on main, runs only on `atalaya`): `origin/main` must be an ancestor of HEAD and
  `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` ⊆ `ci/atalaya-files.txt`.
- Root `.gitlab-ci.yml`: node:24 job → `npm ci` + `bash ci/lint.sh` + `bash ci/test.sh` in
  `tab-recap/`; guard job on `atalaya`. Add `@ast-grep/cli` as a devDependency so CI has ast-grep.

## Step 1 — Bridge out of `main`

- Delete `src/ports/bridge.ts`, `src/adapters/atalaya-bridge.ts` from main (they reappear on atalaya
  under `src/extensions/`).
- `src/recap/render/present.ts`: `BridgeView` → `notes: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly Note[]>` +
  `warnings: readonly string[]` on `ColumnView`; `alertLines` → `noteLines` (render formats `at` with
  the locale's `ago`); `bridgeWarning` → `warningLines`.
- `src/column/main.ts`: build notes/warnings from `extensions(get)` instead of `new AtalayaBridge`.
- `src/daemon/main.ts`: `heal()` loop → `upkeep()` over extensions on the existing `RESYNC_MS` tick.
- `src/daemon/config.ts`: drop `bridgeDir`/`bridgeHeal`; export the `get` used by extensions.
- `bin/tab-recap.ts` `status`: list extensions instead of `bridge …`.
- Generic wording in `rules/recap-no-foreign-write.yml` note, `rules/*` messages, CLAUDE.md,
  CONTEXT.md (**Alert/Heal** → **Note/Upkeep/Extension**), README, `herdr-plugin.toml` description,
  root README "House rules" (no atalaya/delivery-handbook references). `package.json` name
  `@homelab/tab-recap` → `herdr-tab-recap`.

## Step 2 — Any harness writes the recap

- `src/adapters/harnesses.ts`: a table of **profiles** `{ id, command, defaultModel, input: 'stdin'|'argv', invocation(request, model, work) → {args, input, outFile?}, read(ran, outFileText) → {text, costUsd} | null }`.
  - `claude` / `codex`: argv identical to today's `ClaudeSummarizer` / `CodexSummarizer` (golden test).
  - `opencode`, `hermes`: as above; verify flags + a no-tools mode with a live probe before shipping
    each; a profile that cannot be made tool-less is not shipped.
  - `custom`: `TAB_RECAP_CUSTOM_CMD` (split as argv, no shell), prompt on stdin, Markdown on stdout.
- `src/adapters/cli-summarizer.ts`: one `Summarizer` that runs any profile via existing
  `run()`/`scrubbedEnv()` (`src/adapters/run.ts`) and `instructions/message/unfenced`
  (`src/adapters/recap-prompt.ts`). Argv profiles: cap the message at ~100 KiB by trimming the oldest
  excerpt lines (excerpt already keeps the most recent). Delete the two old summarizer files.
- Discovery port `src/ports/harnesses.ts`: `available(): Available | Unknown`; adapter method on
  `HerdrFleet` (RPC `integration.list`), fallback PATH scan in `src/adapters/path-scan.ts`.
- `src/daemon/config.ts`: `Backend` → branded `BackendId` validated against the profile table;
  `TAB_RECAP_BACKEND=auto` (default) → first available in claude → codex → opencode → hermes;
  models `TAB_RECAP_MODEL_<ID>`, legacy `TAB_RECAP_CLAUDE_MODEL` / `TAB_RECAP_CODEX_MODEL` /
  `TAB_RECAP_MODEL` still read. Resolution of `auto` happens in `summarizerFor` (daemon), cached per
  resync, so config stays pure.
- No harness available → the recap error says so and the daemon sends one `notification.show`
  toast per daemon start ("Tab Recap: no summarizer found — run Tab Recap: configure").

## Step 3 — i18n (en/es UI, recap language)

- `src/i18n/messages.ts` (the `Messages` interface + `Locale = 'en' | 'es'`), `en.ts`, `es.ts`
  (`export const es: Messages`) — a missing key fails `tsgo`. Pure data + small functions
  (`ago(ms)`, `needsYou(text)`, hints per `Mode`, badge labels, setup + CLI strings).
  `src/i18n/locale.ts`: `localeOf(value, env)` — `TAB_RECAP_LOCALE=auto|en|es`, auto from
  `LC_ALL`/`LC_MESSAGES`/`LANG`.
- `src/i18n/sections.ts`: `SECTIONS = [{ id: 'goal', en: 'Goal', es: 'Objetivo', hint: {en, es} }, …]`
  for goal · now · waiting · done · decisions · next · refs.
- `present.ts`: every literal moves to `Messages`; `present`, `presentBar`, `footer`, `badge` take
  `m: Messages`; `firstItem(markdown, sectionId)` matches the heading in **any** language.
- `recap-prompt.ts`: instructions generated from `SECTIONS`; `RecapRequest` gains `language`
  (`{ kind: 'known', locale } | { kind: 'free', name }`) and `previousLanguage`; headings in es for
  Spanish, en otherwise; when they differ: "rewrite the whole recap in <language>". Free text is
  sanitised (letters/spaces/hyphen, ≤ 30 chars).
- `TabRecap` (`src/ports/recap-store.ts`, `blankRecap`, fs-recap-store parse) gains
  `language: string | null` (old files → null = en).
- Config: `TAB_RECAP_LOCALE`, `TAB_RECAP_RECAP_LANG=ui|en|es|<name>` in `config.ts` and
  `config.example.env`. Manifest titles stay English (herdr titles are static).
- CONTEXT.md: **Locale**, **Recap language**, **Section**, **Profile**, **Extension**, **Note**,
  **Upkeep** added before use.

## Step 4 — Configure modal

- Manifest: `[[panes]] id = "setup", placement = "popup", command = ["node", "src/setup/main.ts"]`;
  `[[actions]] id = "configure"` → `node bin/tab-recap.ts configure`, which opens it through
  `HerdrFleet` (`plugin.pane.open`, entrypoint `setup`, popup) and on `ui_busy` prints the CLI
  equivalent. Remove `backend-claude` / `backend-codex` actions; keep `backend <id> [model]` CLI.
- `src/setup/form.ts` (pure): state `{rows, cursor, editing, values, availability, testResult}` and
  `step(state, key) → {state, effects}` (effects: `save`, `test`, `close`). Rows: harness (● available
  · ○ not on PATH · ✓ current) · model (free text, default shown) · words · UI language · recap
  language (en / es / free text). Keys: ↑↓/jk, ⏎ edit/confirm, `t` test, `s` save, `q`/Esc close.
- `src/setup/main.ts` (composition root): draws with the `wrap`/`style` helpers from
  `src/recap/render/wrap.ts`, raw-mode stdin like `src/column/main.ts`, saves via `setValues` from
  `bin/set-backend.ts` (move it to `src/adapters/config-file.ts` so the setup root and bin share it),
  test runs one tiny request through `CliSummarizer` and shows seconds/cost or the error.

## Step 5 — Commit, branch, publish

1. `gitleaks detect --no-git` on the tree; first commit on `main` = the public tree after steps 1–4.
2. `git switch -c atalaya`; add the extension files + `ci/atalaya-files.txt` entries; commit.
3. When the operator sends paths: add GitLab remote, push both; GitLab push mirror (protected
   branches only → `main`) to GitHub with a fine-grained token; GitHub topic `herdr-plugin`;
   `herdr plugin install <owner>/<repo>/tab-recap --yes` on a clean HOME to prove it.

## Critical files

`tab-recap/src/adapters/{claude,codex}-summarizer.ts` (→ harnesses.ts, cli-summarizer.ts) ·
`src/adapters/recap-prompt.ts` · `src/adapters/herdr-fleet.ts` · `src/daemon/{config,main}.ts` ·
`src/column/main.ts` · `src/recap/render/present.ts` · `src/ports/{summarizer,recap-store}.ts` ·
`bin/tab-recap.ts`, `bin/set-backend.ts` · `herdr-plugin.toml` · `config.example.env` · `CONTEXT.md`,
`CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, root `README.md` · `rules/*.yml` + probes.

## Verification

- `bash ci/lint.sh` and `bash ci/test.sh` green on both branches; new tests:
  `test/harnesses.test.ts` (golden argv per profile, claude/codex identical to today; argv cap),
  `test/i18n.test.ts` (locale resolution; `firstItem` finds Now/Ahora, Waiting on you/Esperando tu
  respuesta), `test/present.test.ts` updated (notes instead of bridge, es render),
  `test/setup-form.test.ts` (key reducer), `test/config.test.ts` (auto, legacy model keys, recap lang).
- Live on this herdr: `herdr plugin link`, `tab-recap.configure` opens the popup, pick each of
  claude/codex/opencode/hermes, `t` succeeds, a recap is written in Spanish and the phone bar still
  shows "needs you"/Now; switch back to English → full rewrite.
- `main` has no `bridge`/`atalaya` string outside docs of the extension point
  (`grep -ri atalaya tab-recap` empty except CI allowlist); `atalaya` shows the alert header again.
- `ci/branch-guard.sh` fails when a non-allowlisted file is changed on `atalaya` (bite test).

# tab-recap: any harness, configure modal, en/es, and a public `main` without the bridge

## Context

`tab-recap` (herdr plugin, `/home/coder/homelab/herdr-plugins/tab-recap`) writes a rolling recap per
tab, but the summarizer is hard-wired to `claude`/`codex`, configuration is two fixed actions, every
string is English, and the code is coupled to the homelab-only atalaya-bridge (defaults pointing at
`~/.local/state/atalaya-bridge`, heal on via `systemctl --user`). The operator wants to publish the
plugin on GitHub (herdr marketplace) as a mirror of GitLab `main`, keep an `atalaya` flavour for the
homelab, pick the harness from a herdr modal, and have a Spanish/English UI plus a selectable recap
language.

Decisions taken (operator, 2026-10-04): branches **`main` (public) + `atalaya`**, flow main → atalaya
only · harnesses **claude, codex, opencode, hermes + custom** · recap language **en / es / free text**
· scope **recap writer only** (columns stay for claude/codex lanes) · default backend **`auto`** ·
docs **English only** · GitLab/GitHub paths **given later** (mirror is the last step).

Facts measured on herdr 0.9.0 that shape the design:
- herdr has no native form/select UI; a "modal" is a plugin pane with `placement = "popup"` (what
  `HerdrFleet.show` already does). Popup returns `ui_busy` while another herdr modal is open.
- `integration.list` RPC returns `{target, label, command, available, state}` per agent —
  `available` = command on PATH. Here: claude, codex, opencode, hermes. This is discovery.
- `notification.show {title, body}` exists for a first-run toast.
- opencode: `opencode run [message..] --pure -m provider/model --format json`; hermes:
  `hermes -z PROMPT --ignore-rules --ignore-user-config -m MODEL --usage-file PATH` (prints only the
  final text). Both take the prompt as argv → input mode `argv` with a byte cap (MAX_ARG_STRLEN 128 KiB).
- Without the bridge the plugin already degrades (read → `absent`, heal no-ops without a heartbeat);
  the work is removing the coupling, not fixing a crash.
- Repo has **no commits yet** → the first commit on `main` can already be the public tree, so the
  public history never contains the bridge.

## Step 0 — Branch model (built into the code, not just git)

- New generic **Extension** port `src/ports/extension.ts`:
  `{ id; notes?(): NotesResult /* Map<pane, Note{label, at, details[]}> | Unknown */; warning?(m: Messages): string | null; upkeep?(): Promise<UpkeepResult> }`.
  Extensions read their own keys through a `get(key)` handed in (config.ts never learns their keys).
- Registry `src/extensions/index.ts` exports `extensions(get) => []` on `main`. **This is the only
  shared file `atalaya` edits.**
- `atalaya` adds: `src/extensions/atalaya-bridge.ts` (today's `adapters/atalaya-bridge.ts` + the
  `Alert` type from `ports/bridge.ts`, mapped to `Note`), `test/atalaya-bridge.test.ts`,
  `ATALAYA.md`, `config.atalaya.example.env` (bridge dir, heal=1).
- `ci/branch-guard.sh` (on main, runs only on `atalaya`): `origin/main` must be an ancestor of HEAD and
  `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` ⊆ `ci/atalaya-files.txt`.
- Root `.gitlab-ci.yml`: node:24 job → `npm ci` + `bash ci/lint.sh` + `bash ci/test.sh` in
  `tab-recap/`; guard job on `atalaya`. Add `@ast-grep/cli` as a devDependency so CI has ast-grep.

## Step 1 — Bridge out of `main`

- Delete `src/ports/bridge.ts`, `src/adapters/atalaya-bridge.ts` from main (they reappear on atalaya
  under `src/extensions/`).
- `src/recap/render/present.ts`: `BridgeView` → `notes: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly Note[]>` +
  `warnings: readonly string[]` on `ColumnView`; `alertLines` → `noteLines` (render formats `at` with
  the locale's `ago`); `bridgeWarning` → `warningLines`.
- `src/column/main.ts`: build notes/warnings from `extensions(get)` instead of `new AtalayaBridge`.
- `src/daemon/main.ts`: `heal()` loop → `upkeep()` over extensions on the existing `RESYNC_MS` tick.
- `src/daemon/config.ts`: drop `bridgeDir`/`bridgeHeal`; export the `get` used by extensions.
- `bin/tab-recap.ts` `status`: list extensions instead of `bridge …`.
- Generic wording in `rules/recap-no-foreign-write.yml` note, `rules/*` messages, CLAUDE.md,
  CONTEXT.md (**Alert/Heal** → **Note/Upkeep/Extension**), README, `herdr-plugin.toml` description,
  root README "House rules" (no atalaya/delivery-handbook references). `package.json` name
  `@homelab/tab-recap` → `herdr-tab-recap`.

## Step 2 — Any harness writes the recap

- `src/adapters/harnesses.ts`: a table of **profiles** `{ id, command, defaultModel, input: 'stdin'|'argv', invocation(request, model, work) → {args, input, outFile?}, read(ran, outFileText) → {text, costUsd} | null }`.
  - `claude` / `codex`: argv identical to today's `ClaudeSummarizer` / `CodexSummarizer` (golden test).
  - `opencode`, `hermes`: as above; verify flags + a no-tools mode with a live probe before shipping
    each; a profile that cannot be made tool-less is not shipped.
  - `custom`: `TAB_RECAP_CUSTOM_CMD` (split as argv, no shell), prompt on stdin, Markdown on stdout.
- `src/adapters/cli-summarizer.ts`: one `Summarizer` that runs any profile via existing
  `run()`/`scrubbedEnv()` (`src/adapters/run.ts`) and `instructions/message/unfenced`
  (`src/adapters/recap-prompt.ts`). Argv profiles: cap the message at ~100 KiB by trimming the oldest
  excerpt lines (excerpt already keeps the most recent). Delete the two old summarizer files.
- Discovery port `src/ports/harnesses.ts`: `available(): Available | Unknown`; adapter method on
  `HerdrFleet` (RPC `integration.list`), fallback PATH scan in `src/adapters/path-scan.ts`.
- `src/daemon/config.ts`: `Backend` → branded `BackendId` validated against the profile table;

  models `TAB_RECAP_MODEL_<ID>`, legacy `TAB_RECAP_CLAUDE_MODEL` / `TAB_RECAP_CODEX_MODEL` /
  `TAB_RECAP_MODEL` still read. Resolution of `auto` happens in `summarizerFor` (daemon), cached per
  resync, so config stays pure.
- No harness available → the recap error says so and the daemon sends one `notification.show`
  toast per daemon start ("Tab Recap: no summarizer found — run Tab Recap: configure").

## Step 3 — i18n (en/es UI, recap language)

- `src/i18n/messages.ts` (the `Messages` interface + `Locale = 'en' | 'es'`), `en.ts`, `es.ts`
  (`export const es: Messages`) — a missing key fails `tsgo`. Pure data + small functions
  (`ago(ms)`, `needsYou(text)`, hints per `Mode`, badge labels, setup + CLI strings).
  `src/i18n/locale.ts`: `localeOf(value, env)` — `TAB_RECAP_LOCALE=auto|en|es`, auto from
  `LC_ALL`/`LC_MESSAGES`/`LANG`.
- `src/i18n/sections.ts`: `SECTIONS = [{ id: 'goal', en: 'Goal', es: 'Objetivo', hint: {en, es} }, …]`
  for goal · now · waiting · done · decisions · next · refs.
- `present.ts`: every literal moves to `Messages`; `present`, `presentBar`, `footer`, `badge` take
  `m: Messages`; `firstItem(markdown, sectionId)` matches the heading in **any** language.
- `recap-prompt.ts`: instructions generated from `SECTIONS`; `RecapRequest` gains `language`
  (`{ kind: 'known', locale } | { kind: 'free', name }`) and `previousLanguage`; headings in es for
  Spanish, en otherwise; when they differ: "rewrite the whole recap in <language>". Free text is
  sanitised (letters/spaces/hyphen, ≤ 30 chars).
- `TabRecap` (`src/ports/recap-store.ts`, `blankRecap`, fs-recap-store parse) gains
  `language: string | null` (old files → null = en).
- Config: `TAB_RECAP_LOCALE`, `TAB_RECAP_RECAP_LANG=ui|en|es|<name>` in `config.ts` and
  `config.example.env`. Manifest titles stay English (herdr titles are static).
- CONTEXT.md: **Locale**, **Recap language**, **Section**, **Profile**, **Extension**, **Note**,
  **Upkeep** added before use.

## Step 4 — Configure modal

- Manifest: `[[panes]] id = "setup", placement = "popup", command = ["node", "src/setup/main.ts"]`;

  equivalent. Remove `backend-claude` / `backend-codex` actions; keep `backend <id> [model]` CLI.
- `src/setup/form.ts` (pure): state `{rows, cursor, editing, values, availability, testResult}` and
  `step(state, key) → {state, effects}` (effects: `save`, `test`, `close`). Rows: harness (● available
  · ○ not on PATH · ✓ current) · model (free text, default shown) · words · UI language · recap
  language (en / es / free text). Keys: ↑↓/jk, ⏎ edit/confirm, `t` test, `s` save, `q`/Esc close.
- `src/setup/main.ts` (composition root): draws with the `wrap`/`style` helpers from
  `src/recap/render/wrap.ts`, raw-mode stdin like `src/column/main.ts`, saves via `setValues` from
  `bin/set-backend.ts` (move it to `src/adapters/config-file.ts` so the setup root and bin share it),
  test runs one tiny request through `CliSummarizer` and shows seconds/cost or the error.

## Step 5 — Commit, branch, publish

1. `gitleaks detect --no-git` on the tree; first commit on `main` = the public tree after steps 1–4.
2. `git switch -c atalaya`; add the extension files + `ci/atalaya-files.txt` entries; commit.
3. When the operator sends paths: add GitLab remote, push both; GitLab push mirror (protected

   `herdr plugin install <owner>/<repo>/tab-recap --yes` on a clean HOME to prove it.

`tab-recap/src/adapters/{claude,codex}-summarizer.ts` (→ harnesses.ts, cli-summarizer.ts) ·
`src/adapters/recap-prompt.ts` · `src/adapters/herdr-fleet.ts` · `src/daemon/{config,main}.ts` ·

- **Where i18n and sections live.** Use a new top-level `src/i18n/` (`messages.ts`, `en.ts`, `es.ts`, `sections.ts`, `index.ts`). - **The new setup root.** Add `setup` to the `recap-layers-no-io` regex (`#src/(adapters|transport|daemon|column|setup)/`) and `**/src/setup/**` to `recap-no-foreign-write`. Watch identifiers in the key reducer: no `scrollOffset` or `rowOffset`, use `row`/`at`. Spanish UI text like "panel" is fine as a string literal.

`EXCERPT_BUDGET` and `renderExcerpt` count UTF-16 code units, not bytes. Accents take 2 bytes, CJK 3, emoji 4. ## Context

`tab-recap` (herdr plugin, `/home/coder/homelab/herdr-plugins/tab-recap`) writes a rolling recap per

  `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` ⊆ `ci/atalaya-files.txt` (file exists only on atalaya and

1. `gitleaks detect --no-git`; first commit on `main` = steps 1–5 tree (bridge-free).
2. `git switch -c atalaya`: one-line + one-entry edit to `src/extensions/index.ts`; add

   `test/atalaya-bridge.test.ts`, `docs/atalaya.md` (Alert/Heal vocabulary),

3. When the operator sends paths: GitLab remote, push both branches, protect **only `main`**, push

id: recap-domain-pure

  inside:

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/coder/.claude/skills/herdr

# Herdr

Herdr organizes terminals into workspaces, tabs, and panes, recognizes coding agents running inside panes, and exposes the current session through the `herdr` CLI.

Before issuing any control command, verify that this agent is running inside a Herdr-managed pane:

```bash
test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1
```

If the check fails, say that you are not running inside Herdr and stop. Do not inspect or control the focused Herdr session from outside Herdr.

When the check passes, the `herdr` binary in `PATH` talks to the current session. Use it to inspect neighboring work, create terminal layout, start agents and commands, read output, and wait for state changes.

## The CLI is a projection, not the API

**Measured 2026-09-18: `herdr --help` shows a fraction of what Herdr can do.** Two agents in
a row concluded "Herdr has no pub/sub" after reading it. It has: a Unix socket with a
versioned protocol, **102 methods**, **27 subscribable event types** and **26 emitted events**
— and the CLI exposes none of the event surface.

**The schema is the authority, not the binary.** Always start here:

```bash
herdr api schema --json          # the whole protocol, ~275 KB
```

Socket at `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (`~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Newline-delimited JSON:

```
-> {"id":"<opaque>","method":"<method>","params":{}}
<- {"id":"<opaque>","result":{}} | {"id":"...","error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}
```

An **empty `id`** in the reply means Herdr could not even parse the request. That is an
error, not silence — do not treat it as a timeout.

### Events — the part that is not in the CLI

```
events.subscribe   persistent subscription to a list of types
events.wait        blocking wait for ONE event, with timeout_ms
```

A subscription delivers **changes, not the present**: to learn the starting state you still
need one snapshot (`herdr api snapshot`). **An already-blocked lane never changes state**, so
without that snapshot it stays invisible forever.

**Only 3 of the 27 types are per-pane** and require `pane_id`:
`pane.agent_status_changed`, `pane.output_matched`, `pane.scroll_changed`. The other 24 are
global. Watching a whole fleet therefore means subscribing pane by pane and maintaining the
set with `pane.created` / `pane.closed`. `agent_status` is a filter: you can subscribe to
`blocked` only.

`pane.output_matched` is a channel **from inside** a pane: it fires when output matches, so
you can react to any marker a process prints, not just to its status.

## Learn the current CLI

For the subset the CLI does cover:

```bash
herdr --help
```

Then print the relevant command group by running the group without a subcommand:

```bash
herdr agent
herdr pane
herdr workspace
herdr tab
herdr worktree
herdr terminal
herdr notification
herdr integration
herdr session
```

Do not run bare `herdr` for discovery; it launches or attaches the TUI. Do not probe a mutating nested command by omitting arguments. Commands such as `herdr workspace create` are valid with defaults and will execute.

Most control commands return JSON. Read identifiers and state from those responses instead of predicting them.

## Understand layout, panes, and agents

Choose the primitive that matches the job:

- Workspace, tab, and pane topology organize terminal locations.
- Pane commands control raw terminals, shells, tests, servers, input, and output.
- Agent commands control the recognized coding agent currently occupying a pane.

A pane exists whether or not it contains an agent. `agent start` requires an existing available shell pane and never creates, splits, or moves layout. Use pane commands for ordinary processes. Use agent commands when Herdr must validate agent identity or interpret `idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `done`, and `unknown` lifecycle states.

Agent commands accept either a unique live agent name or the pane ID currently hosting that agent. They do not accept terminal IDs or bare agent-kind labels. Names must match `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}` and be unique among live agents. A name follows the current pane occupant and is cleared when that agent exits, is released, or is replaced.

`idle` means the agent is ready for input and its tab has been seen in the focused Herdr UI. `done` is the same underlying idle state after unseen background work finishes. Focusing the tab or targeting the pane or agent with a focus command marks it seen. CLI reads do not mark it seen. `blocked` means Herdr recognized an approval or question UI. `unknown` means an agent is present but Herdr cannot classify it confidently; it does not prove completion.

## Use IDs and caller context

Public IDs are opaque stable handles:

- workspace: `w1`
- tab: `w1:t1`
- pane: `w1:p1`

Closed tab and pane IDs are not reused. A pane moved into another workspace receives a new workspace-qualified pane ID. After `pane move`, continue with `.result.move_result.pane.pane_id` or the live agent name. The old value is reported as `.result.move_result.previous_pane_id`; only the moved process's inherited caller context keeps resolving that old ID, so do not use it as a general agent target.

Herdr injects the caller's context into each managed pane:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID" "$HERDR_TAB_ID" "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Prefer `--current` when a pane command should target the calling pane. Omitting a target may use the UI-focused pane, which can belong to the user or another client.

Discover live state with:

```bash
herdr workspace list
herdr tab list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
herdr pane current --current
herdr pane list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
herdr agent list
```

Creation responses expose the IDs to use next. `workspace create` returns `.result.workspace`, `.result.tab`, and `.result.root_pane`. `tab create` returns `.result.tab` and `.result.root_pane`. `pane split` returns the new pane as `.result.pane`.

## Start and coordinate an agent

Default to a sibling pane in the current tab and the current working directory. Do not create a workspace, tab, worktree, or different cwd unless the user explicitly requests that topology or location.

Honor a direction requested by the user. Otherwise inspect the caller pane:

```bash
herdr pane layout --pane "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Split a wide pane to the right and a narrow or tall pane down. Avoid repeated same-direction splits that create unusably narrow columns or short rows. Keep the user's focus in the calling pane and explicitly preserve the caller's working directory:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Replace `right` with `down` when appropriate. Read the new pane ID from `.result.pane.pane_id`.

An available shell pane must be at its interactive prompt, with the shell itself in the foreground and no foreground command, editor, or agent running. Start a supported agent in that pane with a useful unique name:

```bash
herdr agent start reviewer --kind codex --pane <returned-pane-id>
```

Use the kind requested by the user. Run `herdr agent` to inspect the installed kind list and options. Pass native agent arguments only after `--`:

```bash
herdr agent start reviewer --kind codex --pane <returned-pane-id> -- <agent-args...>
```

A successful `agent start` returns only after Herdr detects the expected agent in the same pane and considers it ready for interactive input. If the agent is blocked during startup, the command returns `agent_not_ready` immediately but keeps the name available for `agent read` and `agent send-keys`. Wait until the agent becomes idle before prompting it. Startup defaults to a 30-second timeout.

Submit work through the agent surface:

```bash
herdr agent prompt reviewer "Review the current diff and report only actionable findings." --wait --timeout 120000
```

`agent prompt` honors the pane's live bracketed-paste mode and sends text followed by encoded Enter after a short delay. It rejects an agent already waiting at an approval or question dialog with `agent_blocked` before sending any input. Inspect the blocked UI and ask the user before answering it. For normal agent work, `--wait` is enough: it waits for the first settled `idle`, `done`, or `blocked` state. Do not repeat those defaults with `--until`.

A prompt sent from a non-working state must produce an observed lifecycle change within five seconds. Otherwise Herdr returns `agent_prompt_stalled` instead of waiting indefinitely. This wait tracks lifecycle state, not an individual turn; if the agent is already working, completion of the active turn may satisfy it.

Use `--until` only for a state-specific workflow, such as waiting for an already-running agent to request input:

```bash
herdr agent wait reviewer --until blocked --timeout 120000
```

Without `--until`, standalone `agent wait` uses the same settled-state defaults as `agent prompt --wait`.

Use logical keys for interactive agent UI controls:

```bash
herdr agent send-keys reviewer esc
herdr agent send-keys reviewer ctrl+c
```

Herdr validates all keys before writing any bytes. Read the result through the resolved agent:

```bash
herdr agent get reviewer
herdr agent read reviewer --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

If a wait fails or returns `blocked`, inspect `agent get` and `agent read` before deciding what input to send. Use the pane surface only when raw terminal control is intentional.

## Run an ordinary command in another pane

Create a sibling pane with the same geometry rule, preserve the caller's working directory, and keep user focus unchanged:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Read the new pane ID from `.result.pane.pane_id`, then run and inspect the command:

```bash
herdr pane run <returned-pane-id> "just test"
herdr pane wait-output <returned-pane-id> --match "test result" --timeout 120000
herdr pane read <returned-pane-id> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

`pane run` atomically sends command text and Enter. `pane wait-output` searches the selected snapshot immediately, so output that already exists can match. Use `--match <text>` for a literal substring or `--regex <pattern>` for a Rust regular expression. Omitting `--timeout` allows an indefinite wait.

Use the read source that matches the task:

- `visible`: the currently rendered viewport.
- `recent`: recent rendered output, including soft wraps.
- `recent-unwrapped`: recent output with soft wraps joined; prefer it for logs and transcripts.
- `detection`: the plain-text bottom-buffer snapshot used for agent detection.

Use `--format ansi` when colors and terminal styling are evidence. Otherwise use text.

`--lines` asks Herdr for more rows from the pane's available screen and host scrollback. If increasing it does not reveal more of a completed response, the pane is probably running the agent on the terminal's alternate screen. Rows that leave the alternate screen do not enter Herdr's host scrollback, so a larger line count cannot recover them.

After that failed read, ask the agent to write its complete response as Markdown in a temporary directory and reply only with the file path, then read the file directly. Use this only as a fallback; do not request file output in the initial prompt.

## Safety and coordination rules

- Use `--no-focus` for background work unless the user asked to switch context.
- Use `--current`, an explicit pane ID, or a unique agent name. Do not rely on another client's focused pane.
- Parse IDs from JSON responses. Do not derive them from sidebar order or examples.
- Do not close workspaces, tabs, panes, or sessions you did not create unless the user explicitly asked.
- Never run `herdr server stop` from an active session unless the user explicitly intends to stop the server and its pane processes.
- Never kill the main Herdr process. Use named test sessions for experiments that need an isolated server.
- CLI server errors are JSON on stderr with exit status 1. CLI syntax errors exit with status 2.

# recap-coder — phase 1 report: PLAN for Step 1 (extension point) + Step 5 (CI)

Status: **plan only — no file in the repo was changed.** I read the prompt as "plan" and the
brief as "stop when the phase is done"; if the reviewer wanted Step 1/5 implemented in this
phase, say so and I implement exactly the list below. Baseline lint/test were not re-run (no
change). Facts below were read from the tree today.

## Surface found (everything that mentions bridge/atalaya/alert/heal)

`src/adapters/atalaya-bridge.ts`, `src/ports/bridge.ts` (delete) · `src/daemon/main.ts`

`bridgeHeal`) · `src/column/main.ts` (`AtalayaBridge`, `bridgeView()`) ·
`src/recap/render/present.ts` (`BridgeView`, `alertLines`, `bridgeWarning`, `STALE_BEAT_MS`) ·
`bin/tab-recap.ts:2,70` · `src/ports/unknowable.ts:3` (comment "the bridge's AD-4") ·
`test/present.test.ts` lines 16, 31–37, 67, 72 · `config.example.env:27-30` ·
`rules/{recap-domain-pure,recap-never-types,recap-no-foreign-write,recap-transport-boundary}.yml`
notes · `ci/lint.sh:36` · `CLAUDE.md:4,37` · `CONTEXT.md:11,25,26` · `README.md:24,28-29` ·
`herdr-plugin.toml:5` · `../README.md:19` · `package.json` + `package-lock.json` (name).
Not in the plan list but found: `unknowable.ts` comment, `bin/tab-recap.ts:2` comment,
`recap-domain-pure.yml` note (ADR-0036), `CONTEXT.md:11` (Lane "same as in atalaya-bridge"),
`package-lock.json` name (two places), `config.example.env`. All included below.

## Step 1 — plan, in order

0. `cp src/adapters/atalaya-bridge.ts src/ports/bridge.ts` → `…/scratchpad/atalaya-stash/`
   (it already holds the originals — verify with `diff`, copy only if absent), then `rm` both.
1. **CONTEXT.md first** (new nouns before code): remove **Alert**, **Heal**; add
   **Extension** (an optional add-on, loaded at startup from `FACTORIES`, that may contribute
   notes, a warning and upkeep; the plugin works with none), **Note** (one labelled line-group
   an extension attaches to a lane, shown under the lane's header), **Upkeep** (the housekeeping
   an extension does on the daemon's resync tick; the column never runs it). Lane row: drop the
   "same word as in atalaya-bridge" sentence. Banned-word table unchanged. Avoid the words
   "bridge/atalaya" everywhere on main.
2. `src/ports/extension.ts` exactly as in the plan: `Note {label; at: number|null;
   details: readonly string[]}`; `NotesResult = {kind:'notes'; byPane: ReadonlyMap<string,
   readonly Note[]>} | Unknown`; `UpkeepResult = {kind:'idle'} | {kind:'acted'; saying: string}
   | Unknown`; `Extension {id; notes?(); warning?(); upkeep?()}`;
   `ExtensionFactory = (get) => Extension | null`. Ports are interfaces only (rule-compatible).
   **Decision:** `warning?(locale)` has no `locale` parameter yet — `Locale` does not exist
   until Step 3 (`src/i18n`); Step 3 adds the parameter (one-line change per implementer). Not
   inventing a placeholder `Locale` type now.
3. `src/extensions/index.ts`: `import type {ExtensionFactory} from '#src/ports/extension.ts';
   export const FACTORIES: readonly ExtensionFactory[] = [];` — never edited on main after.
   (Atalaya later: `import { atalayaBridge } from './atalaya-bridge.ts';` + `[atalayaBridge]`.)
   A second tiny file, `src/extensions/load.ts`, is **not** added; loading is a `.map/.flatMap`
   of two lines in each root (below) — but both roots need the same loop, so put
   `loadExtensions(get): readonly Extension[]` in `src/extensions/load.ts` (3 lines,
   `FACTORIES.flatMap(f => f(get) ?? [])`) to avoid duplicating it. Atalaya's diff stays in
   `index.ts` only.
4. `present.ts`: remove `BridgeView`, `STALE_BEAT_MS`; `ColumnView` gets
   `notes: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly Note[]>` and `warnings: readonly string[]` (import type
   `Note` only, from the port — allowed: render already imports ports). `alertLines` →
   `noteLines(notes, pane, now, width)`: for each note, `wrap('⚑ ' + label + (at===null ? '' :
   ' ' + ago(now-at) + ' ago') + (details.length ? ' · ' + details.join(' · ') : ''),
   width, '  ').map(style.blue)` — byte-identical output to today's alert line when an
   extension supplies label `idle`, details `[branch, '2 unmerged', 'dirty']`.
   `bridgeWarning` → `warningLines(warnings, width)` = each warning wrapped, red, then one `''`
   (only when non-empty). `present`/`presentBar` call sites updated; `presentBar` ignores
   notes/warnings as today ignores bridge.
5. `src/column/main.ts`: drop the AtalayaBridge import/const/`bridgeView`; build
   `const extensions = loadExtensions(get)` where `get` = the re-reading getter (see 6); `view()`
   merges `notes()` of each extension (skip Unknown; merge per-pane arrays in factory order) and
   `warning()` strings (skip null). Reads per 1 s tick like today (extensions own their mtime
   cache). Column never calls `upkeep` (comment says why).
6. `src/daemon/config.ts`: drop `bridgeDir`, `bridgeHeal`, `expandHome` if unused (it is only
   used for bridgeDir → delete; Step 4/5 may re-add), `homedir` stays. Add and export
   `configGetter(): (key: string) => string | undefined` = the `get` closure now inlined in
   `loadConfig` (env wins over config.env, re-read on every call); `loadConfig` uses it.
   `src/daemon/main.ts`: `wire` returns `extensions` (built with `configGetter()`, so an
   extension reads its own `TAB_RECAP_*` keys through the same getter — **re-created per
   resync? No:** built once at start; extension factories that must follow config edits read
   through `get` at call time). The RESYNC tick: `informer.resync(); void upkeep(extensions)`
   where `upkeep` loops `ext.upkeep?.()`, logs `acted` → `log(\`${id}: ${saying}\`)`,
   Unknown → `log(\`${id} upkeep failed: ${saying(why)}\`)`, `idle` silent; never throws
   (try/catch per extension, caught error logged). Keeps `start()` within oxlint max-statements
   25 / 60 lines (move the upkeep loop into its own function, as `heal` is today).
7. Tests (existing + new): update the four `bridge:` call sites in `test/present.test.ts` →
   `notes`/`warnings` (`notes: new Map([['w1:p1', [{label:'idle', at:0, details:['main','2
   unmerged','dirty']}]]])`, same assertions on `⚑ idle`); add: warning line renders red and a
   blank line follows; empty `notes`/`warnings` renders identically to today's no-bridge case.
   `test/extensions.test.ts` (new): `FACTORIES` is empty on main-shape → `loadExtensions` returns
   `[]`; a factory returning `null` is skipped; notes merge across two extensions; Unknown
   notes are skipped; upkeep runner logs acted/unknown and survives a throwing extension (runner
   exported from `src/daemon/upkeep.ts` — a 15-line pure-ish function taking `(extensions,
   log)`, so it is testable without starting the daemon). `config.test.ts`: `configGetter`
   env-over-file and re-read.
   **Present works with zero extensions**: the default path is `notes: new Map()`,
   `warnings: []`; asserted by the first present test and the empty-FACTORIES test.
8. Rules (ast-grep, edit yml + keep probes biting):
   - `recap-no-foreign-write`: add `**/src/extensions/**`, `**/src/i18n/**`, `**/src/setup/**`
     to `files`. Note rewritten: "Transcripts and other tools' files read by an extension are
     READ-ONLY… every write goes through the RecapStore port, the Pidfile adapter or the
     config-file adapter." Caveat to flag: extensions that heal/act may need `run()`, not fs
     writes — fine; if an extension must write it goes behind a port.
   - `recap-layers-no-io`: add `**/src/i18n/**` to `files`; regex →
     `^(node:|#src/(adapters|transport|daemon|column|setup)/)`. Probes: extend `bad.ts` with a
     `#src/setup/…` import so the new alternation provably bites; `good.ts` unchanged.
     **Check:** `recap-layers-no-io` lists only `**/src/recap/**` so far; `src/extensions` is
     deliberately NOT in it (extensions may use adapters/node:).
   - Rewrite the "bridge" prose in `recap-domain-pure` (drop ADR-0036 sentence: "A one-prefix
     test; the domain reaches siblings with './'"), `recap-transport-boundary` (drop the
     generated-client sentence: "so the transport is swappable in one file"),
     `recap-never-types` ("The red line is «no send_keys, ever». Ours is stricter…" →
     drop "bridge's"), `recap-no-foreign-write` (above). `ci/lint.sh:36` → "oxlint (type-aware,
     house configuration)". Also `unknowable.ts:3` comment → "instead of throwing", and
     `bin/tab-recap.ts:2` → "2 usage · 3 could not look".
   - Probe for `src/extensions` coverage of the three rules is via `files` globs; lint.sh runs
     rules on `src bin test`, so the new dir is scanned automatically.
9. Docs/metadata: `CLAUDE.md` layer table + 3 rows (`extensions/` optional add-ons, one file per
   extension, `index.ts` is the only registry; `i18n/`; `setup/`) — the i18n/setup dirs don't
   exist until Steps 3/4, so only `extensions/` goes in now, the other two when created (the
   rules globs for them are harmless to add now). CLAUDE.md line 4 and the red-line row 37
   rewritten without the bridge. `README.md`: replace the "atalaya-bridge aware" bullet with
   "**Extensible.** Optional extensions can add notes under a lane's header and housekeeping
   (see CONTEXT.md)"; line 24 "bridge alert" → "extension notes". Root `README.md`: layering
   bullet → "a pure domain fold, sum-typed ports…" (no atalaya/delivery-handbook); table row
   "written by claude or codex" untouched until Step 2. `herdr-plugin.toml` description: drop
   "plus the lane's atalaya-bridge alert". `config.example.env`: delete lines 27–30.
   `bin/tab-recap.ts status`: replace `bridge …` line with
   `extensions ${loadExtensions(configGetter()).map(e=>e.id).join(', ') || 'none'}`.
   `package.json` and `package-lock.json` name → `herdr-tab-recap` (lockfile edited by
   `npm install --package-lock-only`, which needs network; fallback: sed the two `"name"` lines —
   lockfile equivalent, flagged in the report).
10. Gates: `bash ci/lint.sh`, `bash ci/test.sh` (40 existing, minus nothing, plus the new ones),
    then `grep -rniE 'atalaya|bridge' . ../README.md ../.gitignore --exclude-dir=node_modules
    --exclude-dir=.git` must be empty. (The word "heal" also gone: `grep -rni '\bheal'`.)

### Risks / questions for the reviewer
- `warning?(locale)` deferred to Step 3 (above). Agree?
- `loadExtensions` and `daemon/upkeep.ts` are two small files not in the plan; justification:
  de-dup + testability. Say if you'd rather inline.
- If `Wired.extensions` is built once, an extension never sees a *new* factory-returned `null →
  Extension` transition when config.env changes (e.g. atalaya's `TAB_RECAP_BRIDGE_DIR` set later).
  Alternative: rebuild `loadExtensions` on each resync tick (cheap; extensions then lose
  in-memory state such as the heal rate-limit timestamp → stored on the extension would reset).
  **My choice: build once; extensions re-read `get` per call.** Needs a daemon restart to
  enable/disable an extension — documented in docs.

## Step 5 — plan

State: no `.gitlab-ci.yml`, no `ci/branch-guard.sh`, no `ci/atalaya-files.txt` on main
(correct); `ast-grep` is on PATH here (0.45.3) but not a devDependency; `ci/lint.sh` hard-requires
`command -v ast-grep`. The repo root is `herdr-plugins/` (one level above `tab-recap/`, `.git` is
there), so the CI file sits at `herdr-plugins/.gitlab-ci.yml` and `cd`s into `tab-recap/`.

1. `package.json`: `devDependencies["@ast-grep/cli"]` pinned exact (same style: no ranges),
   version = what `npm view @ast-grep/cli version` returns that is ≥ 0.45 and matches the local
   binary family (0.45.3 if published); `npm install` updates the lock. **`ci/lint.sh`**: replace
   the `command -v ast-grep` check with `AST="$(command -v ast-grep || true)"`; prefer
   `node_modules/.bin/ast-grep` when executable (so CI gets the pinned one, a dev gets the same);
   `AST` used in the 4 call sites; the "NOT COVERED" message names `npm install`. Exit
   semantics unchanged (0/1/3).
2. `herdr-plugins/.gitlab-ci.yml`:
   ```yaml
   default: { image: node:24 }
   stages: [check, guard]
   .tab-recap: { before_script: [cd tab-recap, npm ci] }
   lint: { extends: .tab-recap, stage: check, script: [bash ci/lint.sh] }
   test: { extends: .tab-recap, stage: check, script: [bash ci/test.sh] }
   ```
   plus rules: lint/test on every branch + MRs (`workflow: rules` default, no duplicate MR
   pipelines: run when `$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH` or MR event, not both).
   Guard job:
   ```yaml
   atalaya-branch-guard:
     stage: guard
     variables: { GIT_DEPTH: "0" }
     rules: [{ if: '$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "atalaya"' }]
     script: [bash tab-recap/ci/branch-guard.sh]
   ```
   (node:24 image has git; `bash` present.) `npm ci` needs `package-lock.json` — present.
   Caveat to report: `@typescript/native-preview` + `oxlint-tsgolint` ship platform binaries
   as optional deps; `npm ci` on the Debian image fetches linux-x64 — fine. `ast-grep` npm
   package ships its platform binary the same way.
3. `ci/branch-guard.sh` (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, same exit convention 0/1/3 — 3 = could not
   look: not a git repo, no `origin`, fetch failed). Logic, run from the repo root:
   - `git fetch --quiet origin main` (shallow-safe because `GIT_DEPTH: 0`).
   - `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` else `fail "atalaya is not built on main —
     merge main first"` (exit 1).
   - allowlist file: `tab-recap/ci/atalaya-files.txt` (paths relative to repo root, one per line,
     `#` comments, blank lines ignored). **If the file is absent in HEAD:** not an error for the
     guard's *logic* — absence means the allowlist is empty, so any difference fails; the file is
     expected to exist only on atalaya, and is allowlisted by listing itself.
   - `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` — each name must match an allowlist line
     (exact path match via `grep -Fxq`, no globs → simplest to audit; allowlist lists
     `src/extensions/index.ts`, `src/extensions/atalaya-bridge.ts`, tests, docs, config example,
     itself, … at atalaya time). Offenders printed, exit 1.
   - Env: `GUARD_BASE` (default `origin/main`), `GUARD_ALLOWLIST` (default the path above) to
     make it testable without a remote.
4. **Bite test** `ci/guard-bite.sh` (pattern of `verify-bite.sh`; added to `ci/lint.sh` next to it
   as "the branch guard bites"): in a `mktemp -d` under `${TMPDIR:-…}` (scratchpad when run by
   me; trap-removed) build a throw-away repo: init `main` with one file; branch `atalaya`
   with (a) an allowlisted change → guard must exit 0; (b) a non-allowlisted file change →
   must exit non-zero; (c) a branch not descended from main (orphan commit) → non-zero.
   Uses `GUARD_BASE=main` and a local-only mode: `git fetch` is skipped when
   `GUARD_BASE` doesn't start with `origin/`. It never touches the real repo's state (own
   `GIT_DIR` via `cd`; sets `user.name/email` locally; commit in the scratch repo only — not
   subject to the "no state-changing git" rule, which is about the plugin repo).
   `ci/lint.sh` fails the gate if any of a/b/c misbehaves.
5. Notes for the reviewer: the guard job never runs on main (`rules`), so main CI has no
   dependency on `atalaya-files.txt`; but `ci/guard-bite.sh` runs inside `lint.sh` on both
   branches and creates its own allowlist in the scratch repo, so it passes on main.
   `.gitlab-ci.yml` itself is not in any allowlist: editing it on atalaya fails the guard —
   intended (flow is main → atalaya only).

### Open items not decidable by me
- Real GitLab/GitHub paths (step 6) — unchanged, later.
- Whether `ci/lint.sh` should also run `gitleaks` in CI (not in plan; not added).

## Last lines of lint/test output
Not run — no change made in this phase.
