# recap-coder — tab-recap 1.0.1 (Stability) report

Worktree `/home/coder/homelab/hp-1.0.1` (branch `release/tab-recap-1.0.1`). No git state changed.
**Gates: `bash ci/lint.sh` → lint: clean · `bash ci/test.sh` → 116 pass / 0 fail** (104 → 116, +12).

## Files
- `src/recap/application/informer.ts` — new `reconcile()`: if there is no stream → `enterSubscription()`; otherwise **snapshot only** → push `reconciled` (a failed snapshot is reported via `onBlind`, the live stream is kept). New `tick()` (the daemon's minute beat): every call `resync()`, every `RESUBSCRIBE_EVERY` (10th) a full `enterSubscription()` (half-open safety net). `resync()` (debounced; also what `resync` frames and stream end call) now runs `reconcile()` instead of a full resubscribe. Watch-set change still resubscribes from `run()`; stream death → `pump` end → `resync()` → `reconcile()` sees `stream === null` → resubscribes at once. Optional `resyncDebounceMs` in the existing options object (default 400 ms) for tests.
- `src/daemon/main.ts` — the 60 s interval calls `informer.tick()`.
- `src/transport/herdr.ts` — `subscribe(..., ackTimeoutMs = ACK_TIMEOUT_MS /*10 s*/)`: no ack in time → reject `events.subscribe: no ack in N ms` + destroy the socket → the existing informer backoff path. Timer cleared on ack, error reply, socket error and close.
- `src/adapters/run.ts` — child spawned `detached` (own process group); on timeout SIGTERM to the **group**, SIGKILL to the group after `killAfterMs` (new optional `RunOptions`, default 5 s); the promise **always resolves** (after SIGKILL immediately with code 137, and 1 s after the program's `exit` even if a grandchild still holds the pipes; stdio destroyed). `killGroup` never calls `kill(-0)` (guarded when `pid` is undefined). New `export type Runner = typeof run`.
- `src/adapters/opencode-summarizer.ts` — injectable `runner` (+ `relistMs`, default 3 s) in the constructor; `forget()`: id printed → delete by id; no id (killed/timed out) → list by title → delete, wait `relistMs`, **one** more list → delete.
- `CONTEXT.md` — **Reconcile** row says a refresh of a subscribed daemon takes only the snapshot, and when a subscription is opened.
- `../CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased]` Changed (minute refresh no longer resubscribes) + Fixed (ack timeout, process-group kill, EPIPE, opencode leak). No version heading/bump.

## Tests (new files)
- `test/informer-reconcile.test.ts` (4) — a `CountingHerdr` fake: nine ticks = no new subscription but nine snapshots, the 10th tick resubscribes; a `resync` frame → +1 snapshot, 0 subscriptions; stream death → resubscribes without waiting for a tick; a new lane (watch-set change) resubscribes, a status change does not.
- `test/run-process.test.ts` (5) — behaviour unchanged (output/exit code/missing program → 127); a program that **ignores SIGTERM** and has a `sleep` child is SIGKILLed with its group (grandchild verified dead); `sh -c 'sleep 30 & echo done; exit 0'` resolves in well under 5 s; subscribe against a silent unix socket rejects `no ack in 80 ms`; a program that exits without reading 2 MB of stdin does not crash (EPIPE).
- `test/opencode-leak.test.ts` (3) — scripted runner: timeout with no session id → `session list --format json` → `session delete <id>` (someone else's session never touched); a session that appears only after the kill is caught by the **one** delayed re-list (exactly two lists); id printed → deleted by id with no listing.
- Before-fix evidence: the informer tests need `tick()`/`reconcile` (absent) and the "resync frame does not resubscribe" case cannot hold with the old `resync()`; the old `run()` I checked directly — it **crashes the whole process with `Error: write EPIPE`** when the child exits before reading stdin (that is the trace in the old `daemon.log`), so the fifth test/bullet is a real fix, not hardening. I did not re-run the new tests against the old tree wholesale (no git state changes allowed).

## Decisions the plan did not fix
- `tick()` is a new public method rather than a flag on `resync()`, so frames and ticks are told apart for the 10th-tick counter; `resync()` kept as the debounced entry point.
- `reconcile()` with a live stream and a failed snapshot does **not** schedule a retry (the next tick retries; a dead stream is handled by `pump`); with no stream the existing backoff applies.
- `run()` EXIT grace is a fixed 1 s (not configurable): long enough for the pipes to drain after a normal exit, short enough not to stall the recap job.
- `run()` now detaches children from the daemon's process group: a daemon killed hard no longer takes an in-flight summarizer with it (it ends by its own timeout).
- Fake-time was not used; the tests use millisecond-scale options so they finish in ~1–2 s each.

## Not done / not claimed
- The "≤ 1 `tab-recap:sub` per 10 min at steady state" acceptance is **not measured live** (the live daemon runs the old code; I did not touch it). By construction it is one subscription per 10 ticks plus watch-set changes and stream death.
- macOS is not claimed here, as instructed. The column toggle was not started.

## Last lines of output
```
lint: clean
ℹ tests 116
ℹ pass 116
ℹ fail 0
```

39a50d5 tab-recap: stability — reconcile without resubscribing, ack timeout, kill process groups
### [Unreleased]

#### Changed

- The once-a-minute refresh no longer opens a new event subscription (herdr logged one stream per minute for nothing): it takes a snapshot only. A new subscription is opened when the watch set changes, when the stream ends, and on every 10th minute as a safety net against a half-open connection.

#### Fixed

- A subscription that herdr never acknowledges is abandoned after 10 seconds and retried with backoff, instead of hanging.
- A summarizer that times out is killed with its whole process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 seconds), and a grandchild that keeps the pipes open can no longer hold the daemon waiting forever.
- A program that exits without reading its input (for example a missing or crashing harness) no longer crashes the daemon with `write EPIPE`.
- opencode: a run killed before it reported its session id has its stored session found by title and deleted, with one more look a few seconds later in case opencode was still writing it.

+#### Changed

+- The once-a-minute refresh no longer opens a new event subscription (herdr logged one stream per minute for nothing): it takes a snapshot only. A new subscription is opened when the watch set changes, when the stream ends, and on every 10th minute as a safety net against a half-open connection.

First public release.

- A pane is taken for a recap column only if its title is exactly `tab-recap` or `tab-recap:bar`, it hosts no agent and, when herdr reports one, its label is the manifest's. Before, any pane whose title merely *started with* `tab-recap` (for example an agent session named `tab-recap-harness-config`) was adopted as a column and closed with the columns when the daemon stopped.

- A recap never closes, resizes or moves a pane that hosts an agent: enforced where the board adopts columns, in the close-column intents, and at the herdr edge, which checks the pane in a fresh snapshot before `pane.close`, `pane.resize` and `pane.swap` and refuses (with a log line) if it hosts an agent.

content.text:
The fixed recap structure is in the plan for 1.1.0, and **1.0.1 is released and deployed**.

**Fixed recap structure (1.1.0):**
- **Sections:** always all seven, in this order: Goal · Now · Needs you · Done · Decisions · Next · Links. In Spanish: Objetivo · Ahora · Te necesita · Hecho · Decisiones · Siguiente · Enlaces. An empty section shows "—".
- **Length caps, enforced by code:** Goal is one line; at most 3 bullets in Now and Needs you, 5 in Done and Next, 3 in Decisions, 6 in Links; at most 16 words per bullet.
- **How it's guaranteed:** the model returns data rather than Markdown, the plugin trims it to the caps and builds the recap itself. The prompt asks for plain words, short sentences and real names (files, branches, MR numbers). An invalid answer is retried once, then the previous recap stays.
- **Phone bar:** reads "Needs you" (or else "Now") directly.
- **Retired:** the "Words" setting; the caps replace it.
- **Tasks:** 1.2's tasks reuse the same fixed block, one per task.

**1.0.1 is released:**
- **Releases:** on both GitHub and GitLab, from tag `tab-recap-v1.0.1`, with notes taken from the changelog.
- **What's in it:**
  - The minute tick no longer resubscribes. The old daemon made 42 subscriptions in about 30 minutes.
  - A 10-second subscribe timeout.
  - A timed-out harness is killed together with any processes it started.
  - A test proves opencode leaves no session behind.
  - A real crash fixed: the daemon died with `write EPIPE` whenever a harness exited before reading its input.
- **Branches:** `atalaya` has 1.0.1 merged in. The guard is clean and its 121 tests pass.
- **Daemon:** redeployed with a normal stop/start, and all 30 agent panes survived. A 12-minute measurement of the new subscription rate is running in the background.

**Now running:**
- **ship-1-1:** the 1.1 tooling (GitHub CI, release automation, changelog check, screenshots). Still at work on the screenshot fixtures.
- **recap-coder:** the `prefix+r` column toggle, on its own branch from `main` at 1.0.1. The fixed recap structure comes after that.

I'll review each one when it reports back, and 1.1.0 ships once all three pieces are merged.

content.text:
Not yet. For 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 I did both steps by hand: I created and pushed the tag, then created the GitHub release with `gh` and the GitLab release through the API.

**From 1.1.0**, the release step becomes automatic and the tag stays manual:

| Step | 1.0.x (now) | From 1.1.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decide to release: changelog section + version bump | by hand (me) | by hand (me) |
| Create and push the tag `tab-recap-vX.Y.Z` | by hand (me) | by hand (me) |
| GitLab release with notes | by hand (API) | **automatic**: GitLab CI tag pipeline |
| GitHub release with notes | by hand (`gh`) | **automatic**: GitHub Actions on the mirrored tag |
| Check that the versions match the tag | none | **automatic**: release fails on a mismatch |

**The tag itself could be automatic too.** A job on GitLab `main` would create the tag whenever a commit raises the version in `herdr-plugin.toml` and no tag exists for it yet. Releasing would then just mean merging a commit that bumps the version and dates the changelog section.
- **Cost:** GitLab's built-in CI token can't push tags, so it needs a project access token with write access to the repository, stored as a masked CI variable.
- **Where it runs:** on GitLab only, because GitHub is just a mirror and anything created there directly gets out of sync.

Should I add automatic tagging to 1.1.0? If yes, create the project access token in GitLab and I'll wire it up.

message.content: How do we make sure the pipeline releases a proper release tag?

content.text:
Tags are already protected in GitLab (`tab-recap-v*`), so only Maintainers can create them. On top of that, one script, `ci/check-release.sh <tag>`, runs before any release is published, in both GitLab CI and GitHub Actions. It fails the pipeline if any of these checks fails:

| Check | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Name** | matches `tab-recap-vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` exactly (semantic version, no leading zeros, no stray suffix) |
| **Kind** | annotated tag, not a plain one, so it records who tagged and a message |
| **Commit** | points at a commit that is on `main`, never a release branch or `atalaya` |
| **Order** | newer than the previous `tab-recap-v*` tag, so no duplicates or going backwards |
| **Versions** | `herdr-plugin.toml`, `package.json` and `package-lock.json` all equal the tag's version |
| **Changelog** | a dated, non-empty `### [x.y.z] — YYYY-MM-DD` section exists, sits under `[Unreleased]`, and has its link line |
| **Gates** | lint and tests pass on the tagged commit; on GitHub, Ubuntu **and** macOS must pass before the release job runs |
| **Manifest** | `herdr-plugin.toml` parses, has the required fields, and every action and pane points to a file that exists |
| **No overwrite** | the job stops if a release for the tag already exists; tags are never moved, and a bad release is fixed by the next patch |

The release notes are cut from that changelog section, and the release is only created after every check above passes.

**Proving the checks work:** like the existing lint rules, `check-release.sh` gets a test with deliberately bad tags that must fail: a wrong name, a lightweight tag, a tag off `main`, a version mismatch, a missing changelog section, a tag older than the last one. That way the gate is proven able to block a bad tag, not just assumed to.

**With automatic tagging:** the tag job on `main` runs the same script *before* it creates the tag, so a malformed tag can't be created in the first place.

**After publishing:** GitHub's release job repeats the checks on the mirrored tag. If GitLab and GitHub ever disagree, for example a tag pointing at a different commit, it fails visibly instead of publishing.

ship-1-1 is already building `check-version.sh` and `release-notes.sh` for 1.1. I'll widen that into `check-release.sh` with every check above plus its bad-tag test, and send it to ship-1-1 as soon as it reports back on its current work. I'm not interrupting it mid-task.

Worktree `/home/coder/homelab/hp-toggle` (branch `feat/tab-recap-column-toggle`, from main d5d2c85). No git state changed; versions not bumped.

## Model (domain, pure)
- `Board` gains `hidden: Set<TabId>`, `allHidden: boolean` and **`shown: Set<TabId>`** (the plan named only the first two; "all hidden, then show one" needs the exceptions set). Rule, in one place (`src/recap/domain/visibility.ts`): `isHidden(board, tab) = allHidden ? !shown.has(tab) : hidden.has(tab)`.
- Observations: `{kind:'visibility', target: {tab} | 'all', hidden}` and `{kind:'hidden-restored', state}` (what was saved, fed at start). New intent `{kind:'save-hidden', state}` (Dispatch → `store.writeHidden`; `Dispatch.send` failed to compile until handled, as designed).
- `policy.ts`: `deserves()` needs `!isHidden`, `closed()` closes the column of a hidden tab → hide = `close-column` now, show = `open-column` (the existing settle); a column we closed that then reports `closed` finds no column on the board, so **nothing is spent from the reopen budget and nothing is given up** while hidden. Reconcile never adopts/keeps a column in a hidden tab (closes a found one). Recaps/publish are untouched (still requested on turn end, focus, `r`).
- Showing a tab (or all) also **forgets its reopen history and give-up** (the operator's word beats the daemon's give-up) — not in the plan; flagged below.
- `all` hidden=true sets the blanket and clears `hidden`/`shown`; with the blanket on, "hide one" removes it from `shown`; `all` hidden=false clears everything. Tabs that appear later under the blanket start hidden.
- `fold.ts`: `route` was over oxlint's complexity limit, so focused/requested/switched/visibility/hidden-restored moved to `onOperator()` (own exhaustive `never` switch).

## State, requests, actions
- Port `RecapStore`: `readHidden`/`writeHidden` (`HiddenState {all, hidden[], shown[]}`, `NOTHING_HIDDEN`) and `requestVisibility`/`takeVisibility` (`VisibilityRequest {target: 'all'|tabId, hidden}`). `FsRecapStore`: `hidden.json` in the state dir (written atomically; missing/garbage → nothing hidden; wrong-typed fields dropped); requests are one JSON file each in `visibility/`, named `<ms>-<pid>-<n>.json`, taken **in order and removed**, junk deleted.
- Daemon: pushes `hidden-restored` (from `hidden.json`) right after wiring and **before** the first subscription/reconcile, and the existing 1 s request poll also drains `takeVisibility()` into `visibility` observations. Dispatch persists every change via `save-hidden`.
- `bin/tab-recap.ts`: `column` (this tab: `HERDR_PLUGIN_CONTEXT_JSON` → current tab) and `columns` read the saved state, decide hide vs show (`hiddenIn()` / `saved.all`), write one request, print en/es. Manifest: `tab-recap.column` (contexts tab/pane) and `tab-recap.columns`.
- Column process: `h` writes a hide request for its tab (works in the column and in the modal — the modal stays open, the column goes away); footer hints in en/es mention it (the shortest variants still fit a phone column).
- Messages (en/es): `cli.columnHidden/columnShown/columnsHidden/columnsShown`, hints.

## Docs
`tab-recap/README.md` (action rows, `h` key, key-binding example: `prefix+r` → `tab-recap.column`, `prefix+shift+r` → `tab-recap.columns`), root `README.md` (the actions sentence), `CONTEXT.md` (**Hidden** term; Observation/Intent rows list the new members), `../CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` → Added.

## Tests
`test/visibility.test.ts` (11): golden fold sequences — hide→close+save, show→open+save; hidden does not spend the reopen budget (6 close events after hiding: no give-up, no open, `reopens` empty); hidden ignores reconcile (found column closed, none opened); recaps still asked while hidden (requested + turn-ended); all-hidden → new tab stays hidden → show one → show all (exact saved states at each step); hide-again under the blanket; restored-at-start respected by the first reconcile; show forgets give-up; `hiddenState`/`restoreHidden` round-trip + `hiddenIn`; store `hidden.json` round-trip incl. garbage/wrong types; visibility requests taken once, in order, junk dropped. `recap-job.test.ts` fake store updated for the new port methods.

## Decisions / things to check
- `shown` set added to the board (see above); `HiddenState` is `{all, hidden, shown}` on disk.
- Show forgives give-up/reopens (not in the plan).
- The toggle decision is made in the CLI from the **saved** state (`hidden.json`), not the live board: two presses within the daemon's 1 s poll both read the same state and send the same request (idempotent, so the second press may look like a no-op). Acceptable at human speed.
- A bar-shaped tab shown again opens its bar only when focused (existing dock rule); not changed.
- The **root** README's key example still binds `prefix+r` to `tab-recap.configure` while the tab-recap README now suggests `prefix+r` for the toggle — I left the root example alone (docs-only, "use any free key"); you may want to change it to avoid a conflict.
- Not done live (daemon runs old code; I did not touch it, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` or the bindings, as instructed).

content.text:
Both wave-1 pieces passed my first read: the column toggle (127/127 tests) and the 1.1 tooling (107/107). Your switch to MR-based releases changes how they land, so first my answer on the runner:

**Use LiteLLM, but not on `deploy-infra-runner`.** Run the release-notes job on **`k8s-runner-homelab`**: it already runs our lint and tests, and it's in the same k3s cluster as LiteLLM (`llm.devel.crisaac.dev`).
- **Why not `deploy-infra`:** it's your Proxmox infrastructure deploy runner, so it holds the most powerful credentials you have. This job feeds MR descriptions to an LLM, and anyone who can write an MR description can try to steer that model. Least privilege says keep that job away from infra secrets.
- **Why LiteLLM:** codex talks to `https://llm.devel.crisaac.dev/v1` with a **LiteLLM virtual key** limited to one model and a small budget. No OpenAI key enters GitLab, and LiteLLM logs every call and caps the spend.
- **Damage control:**
  - codex runs read-only, with no tools, in a throwaway container
  - its output only counts after `check-release.sh` validates it: fixed template, every bullet cites a real MR, and the version comes from labels, not from the model

**What changes in the plan because of MR-based releases:**
- **Changelog check:** ship-1-1's check that a change touched `CHANGELOG.md` becomes a check that **the MR carries one `changelog::` label and a filled-in description template**. The release agent then writes `CHANGELOG.md` itself, from the MRs.
- **Release pipeline additions (ship-1-1):**
  - the MR template and labels
  - the version decided from labels
  - the codex-via-LiteLLM notes job
  - automatic commit and tag
  - the expanded `check-release.sh`
- **Order for 1.1.0:**
  1. tooling MR
  2. toggle MR
  3. fixed-structure MR
  4. release-pipeline MR
  5. then **1.1.0 is released by the new pipeline itself**, as its first real test.
- **Toggle fix:** the root README's example binds `prefix+r` to `configure`. That becomes the toggle, so the docs don't contradict your keys.

Two things I need from you:

date: 2026-08-01

# ADR-065: Infisical as the single source of truth for GitLab CI/CD secrets (Secret Sync)
<!-- MADR 4.0 — https://adr.github.io/madr/ -->
## Context and Problem Statement
GitLab CI/CD secrets lived as **hand-set project/group variables**, scattered across every repo in the
`homelab` group (26 across 9 repos + the group). There was no single source of truth: rotating a token meant
editing GitLab by hand per repo, values were invisible to Infisical (our declared secrets vault), and there
was no audit trail. How do we make **Infisical the one source of truth** for CI secrets **without reworking
the pipelines** (which already read plain CI env vars like `$TF_VAR_PROXMOX_API_TOKEN`)?
## Decision Drivers
* Single source of truth — Infisical owns the value; GitLab is a projection.
* Zero pipeline churn — jobs keep reading normal CI/CD variables; no `infisical run` wrapper required.
* Self-hosted on both ends — GitLab (`gitlab.devel.crisaac.dev`) and Infisical (`secrets.infra.crisaac.dev`).
* Least privilege + auditability; don't clobber existing working variables during migration.
## Considered Options
* **A. Infisical Secret Sync (push)** — Infisical pushes secrets to GitLab CI/CD variables automatically.
* **B. Pipeline pull (`infisical run`)** — each job installs the Infisical CLI and pulls secrets at runtime;
  secrets never persist in GitLab.
* **C. Status quo** — keep hand-set GitLab CI/CD variables.
## Decision Outcome
Chosen option: **A (Secret Sync, push)**, because it makes Infisical authoritative while the pipeline is
**unchanged** (the sync writes the same CI/CD variables the jobs already consume). Verified that the
self-hosted Infisical supports a GitLab **App Connection** with a custom `instanceUrl` (B was the documented
fallback only if push didn't work self-hosted; it does). B stays available for jobs that want zero footprint
in GitLab.
### How it is wired
* **One App Connection** `gitlab-iac-sync` (method `access-token`, `instanceUrl=https://gitlab.devel.crisaac.dev`)
  using a **`homelab` group access token** (`api` scope, Owner) — so it can manage CI/CD variables for **any**
  repo in the group and the group itself.
* **Secrets live in Infisical** project **`infrastructure`** (slug `infrastructure-n5-tg`), env `prod`,
  mirroring the GitLab hierarchy:
  - `/gitlab-ci/homelab` → GitLab **group** variables (shared: `CI_REGISTRY_*`, `FLUX_BOT_TOKEN`, `LITELLM_*`).
  - `/gitlab-ci/homelab/<repo>` → that GitLab **project**'s variables.
* **One Secret Sync per destination** (group + 9 repos = 10), each with `disableSecretDeletion: true`
  (Infisical never deletes a GitLab variable) and `shouldMaskSecrets: true`.
### Amendment 2026-08-27 — CI secrets relocated to the `infrastructure` project
Originally these lived in the project whose **slug** is `k3s-platform` — which the UI
displays as **`k3s-greece`**, the production Kubernetes cluster's secret project. That
was a semantic error: CI/CD variables for infrastructure repositories are not workloads
of the production cluster, and parking them there meant an operator opening the obvious
project (`infrastructure`, or `k3s-homelab`) found *"This project has no syncs
configured"* while the syncs lived somewhere unrelated.
All **12** syncs and **36** secrets were migrated to the `infrastructure` project on
2026-08-27. Method, for future moves: copy every secret and verify by SHA-256 per key,
then per destination `DELETE .../secret-syncs/gitlab/<id>?removeSecrets=false` (the
parameter is required, and `false` leaves the GitLab variables in place) followed by
re-creating the sync against the new project. Group-scoped sync last — widest blast
radius. GitLab CI variables were unchanged throughout; no pipeline was affected.
**API gotchas found doing it:** the DELETE endpoint returns HTTP 500 if a
`Content-Type: application/json` header is sent without a body; `destinationConfig`
requires `projectName` as well as `projectId` on create; and secret values are
frequently **multiline** (`VPS_SSH_KEY`, `KUBECONFIG`) — copy them as JSON, never by
line-based shell parsing, or values are truncated and fragments become secret *names*.
### Conventions & gotchas
* **Change a secret** → edit it in Infisical `/gitlab-ci/homelab/<repo>`; it syncs automatically. **Never**
  set the GitLab CI/CD variable by hand.
* **Onboard a repo** → create the folder + a project-scoped Secret Sync (the group connection already covers it).
* **Masking is per-sync (all-or-nothing).** GitLab cannot mask **multiline** (`KUBECONFIG`), **<8-char**
  (`OPENFAAS_USER`), or values with disallowed characters like **`!`** — the Proxmox token format
  `user@realm!id=secret` is rejected ("value is invalid") on a fresh masked create (existing ones like
  greece's are *grandfathered*). Those syncs use `shouldMaskSecrets: false`. A destination mixing maskable +
  unmaskable secrets must **split**: e.g. `homelab/IaC` uses `iac-ci-vars` (mask=true: `AWS_*`) plus
  `ci-iac-nomask` on subpath `/gitlab-ci/homelab/IaC/nomask` (mask=false: `TF_VAR_MYCENAE_PROXMOX_API_TOKEN`).
  Syncs are **non-recursive**, so a subpath is a clean separate sync.
* **Project naming trap**: Infisical project slugs and display names differ. The CI
  secrets project is displayed as **`infrastructure`** (slug `infrastructure-n5-tg`,
  id `0b51eba5-…`). Syncs are visible under that project → *Integrations → Secret Syncs*;
  they are not shown in `k3s-homelab` or `k3s-greece`.
* **Group-level variables are readable by every repo's CI in the group** — keep sensitive tokens at the
  **project** path, not the group path.
* `disableSecretDeletion: true` means deleting a secret in Infisical does **not** remove the GitLab variable —
  delete it in GitLab manually too.
### Consequences
* Good — one place to rotate/audit CI secrets; pipelines untouched; onboarding a repo is one sync.

# gitlab-webhooks — function invariants

The central **GitLab group-webhook hub** for the `homelab` group. One HTTP trigger
(`/gitlab-webhooks`) receives every group webhook; `handler.py` authenticates and
parses, then `dispatch.py` routes by `object_kind` to a handler under `handlers/`.
There is **no per-repo CI step** — the group webhook fans every repo in here.

First handler: `release_highlights` (`object_kind: release`, `action: create`) —
generates an AI "Highlights" block (litellm → `minimax-m3`) and prepends it to the
new release's notes. Add a webhook type = one module under `handlers/` + one entry
in `dispatch._REGISTRY`.

## Non-obvious rules

- **Thin composition root.** `handler.py` owns only auth + parse + dispatch. Every
  domain decision (which action, which fields, which prompt) lives in the handler
  module. Shared clients (`gitlab_client`, `litellm_client`) are generic and
  prompt-free — the system prompt is the handler's concern.
- **Stateless.** No DB, no `store`, no `schema.sql`, no bootstrap Job. The release
  handler's idempotency is checked against the release description itself
  (`service.HIGHLIGHTS_MARKER`).
- **Best-effort.** Any handler failure returns `200 {"status":"error"}` and logs —
  never a 5xx (GitLab would retry-storm). Unknown/uninteresting payloads return
  `200 {"status":"ignored"}`.
- **Auth is `X-Gitlab-Token`** (the webhook secret), compared with `hmac.compare_digest`.
- **Secrets are files** (matching filename ↔ Secret key ↔ InfisicalSecret template):
  `gitlab-webhooks-webhook-secret`, `gitlab-webhooks-litellm-key`, `gitlab-webhooks-gitlab-token`.
- The GitLab token needs `api` scope (it PUTs release descriptions across the group).
- **Prompt** lives in `handlers/release_highlights.SYSTEM_PROMPT` (one place,
  versioned, serves all repos). Migrating it to a litellm server-side `prompt_id` is
  a later option.

HIGHLIGHTS_MARKER = "## ✨ Highlights"


def add_highlights(project_id: int, tag: str, gitlab: GitLab, highlighter: Highlighter) -> str:
    """Prepend an AI 'Highlights' block to a release. Pure orchestration over injected ports."""
    current = gitlab.release_description(project_id, tag)
    if HIGHLIGHTS_MARKER in current:
        return "already-present"

    previous = gitlab.previous_tag(project_id, tag)
    if previous is None:

    subjects = gitlab.commit_subjects(project_id, previous, tag)
    if not subjects:

    block = f"{HIGHLIGHTS_MARKER}\n\n{highlights}\n\n---\n\n"
    gitlab.set_release_description(project_id, tag, block + current)
    return "updated"

---
name: release-highlights-hub
description: How AI release highlights work in the homelab group (Fission gitlab-webhooks hub) and the two onboarding traps per repo
metadata:
  type: reference
---

AI release notes in the `homelab` GitLab group come from the Fission function `homelab/serverless-functions` → `functions/gitlab-webhooks` (handler `release_highlights`): on a release `create` event it asks LiteLLM (`minimax-m3`) for 3–6 bullets from **commit subjects** between the previous tag and the new one and prepends `## ✨ Highlights`. Logs: `kubectl --context k3s-homelab -n fission-fn logs <container-gitlab-webhooks-…>`. It always answers 200 (`{"status":"error"}` on failure), so failures are silent.

Per-repo onboarding traps (found 2026-10-04 on homelab/herdr-plugins):
1. GitLab here is CE (no group webhooks): each project needs a **project webhook** to `http://router.fission.svc.cluster.local/gitlab-webhooks`, releases events only, token = Infisical `k3s-homelab-chxh` prod `/faas/functions/gitlab-webhooks/WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
2. The hub's token is the `homelab` group bot with **Developer** role: protected tags must allow Developers to create, or editing the release returns 403.

CI secrets follow ADR-065 (Infisical `infrastructure` prod `/gitlab-ci/homelab/<repo>` + one Secret Sync per repo); the operator wants **every** GitLab CI variable synced from Infisical, never hand-set. See [[tab-recap-branches]].

content.text:
Yes, the function works, and now it works for `herdr-plugins` too. The 1.0.1 GitLab release has its `## ✨ Highlights` block.

**Why it hadn't worked for us:**
1. **No webhook:** your GitLab is Community Edition, which has no group webhooks, so the "group hub" is really one project webhook per repo. `homelab-cli` has one; `herdr-plugins`, being new, didn't. I added it (releases only, same URL), using the webhook secret from Infisical (`k3s-homelab` → `/faas/functions/gitlab-webhooks`).
2. **403 on saving, my own doing:** I had made `tab-recap-v*` tags creatable by Maintainers only. GitLab applies that rule to editing a release too, and the function's group bot is a Developer. The function read the release and generated the text, then got 403 on save. I lowered tag creation to **Developers + Maintainers**. Tags stay protected, so they can't be moved or deleted. I didn't raise the bot to Maintainer, since that would apply to every repo in the group.

After both fixes, a replayed release event produced the Highlights on 1.0.1. The function always answers 200, so it fails silently: that's why I read its logs in the cluster (`fission-fn` namespace).

**On the variables:** agreed, and that's the current state. `herdr-plugins` has exactly one CI variable, `RELEASE_TOKEN`, pushed from Infisical by the `ci-herdr-plugins` sync; nothing is set by hand. The webhook isn't a CI variable but a project setting, and its secret came straight from Infisical.

**Quality:** one bullet is inaccurate. The function says the subscribe timeout stops "the summarizer getting stuck waiting on unresponsive tabs", which isn't what it does. That's the commit-subjects input showing its limits, and the reason to have the function read MR titles and descriptions instead, as you suggested.

**Two follow-ups worth doing:**
- **Function upgrades:** read merged MRs instead of commit subjects, and use one tag series per plugin. Both would happen in `serverless-functions` through its own agent and MR.
- **Onboarding:** make repo setup add the webhook and the Infisical sync together, so the next new repo doesn't miss them.

I saved both setup traps (per-repo webhook, tags creatable by Developers) to memory.

Still pending on our side:
- the column toggle and the 1.1 tooling, both reviewed and ready to land through MRs under the new flow
- recap-coder, idle, with your unsent "The fixed recap structure — go ahead" in its input box
